title: Stalks of extension by zero of modules on a ringed space, and the maps between them
statement: Let $(X,\mathcal O_X)$ be a ringed space [def-weil-locally-ringed-space-morphism] and $F$ a sheaf of $\mathcal O_X$-modules [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. For an open $W\subseteq X$ with inclusion $j_W$ write $j_{W,!}:\operatorname{Mod}(\mathcal O_X|_W)\to\operatorname{Mod}(\mathcal O_X)$ for extension by zero, the left adjoint of restriction [lem-sc-derived-open-restriction-adjunction-exact], and use stalks as in [def-weil-pbc-module-stalk]. (1) For an $\mathcal O_X|_W$-module $G$ and $x\in X$: if $x\notin W$ then $(j_{W,!}G)_x=0$; if $x\in W$ there is an isomorphism of $\mathcal O_{X,x}$-modules $G_x\cong(j_{W,!}G)_x$, natural in $G$. (2) For opens $W\subseteq W'\subseteq X$ there is a canonical morphism of $\mathcal O_X$-modules $\iota_{W,W'}:j_{W,!}(F|_W)\to j_{W',!}(F|_{W'})$, adjoint to the restriction to $W$ of the unit $F|_{W'}\to(j_{W',!}(F|_{W'}))|_{W'}$ of the adjunction (with $j_{X,!}$ the identity functor and identity unit); $\iota_{W,X}$ is the counit $j_{W,!}(F|_W)\to F$ of the adjunction, $\iota_{W,W}$ is the identity, and $\iota_{W',W''}\circ\iota_{W,W'}=\iota_{W,W''}$ for $W\subseteq W'\subseteq W''$. (3) For $x\in W$, under the isomorphisms of (1) with $G=F|_W$ and $G=F|_{W'}$ (and $(F|_{W'})_x=F_x=(F|_W)_x$), the stalk $(\iota_{W,W'})_x$ is the identity of $F_x$.

source.place: Sheaves Tag 00A7 (sheaves-lemma-j-shriek-modules), clauses (2)-(4), and the definition of $j_{p!}$ for presheaves of modules preceding it

proof.text: For an $\mathcal O_X|_W$-module $G$ let $P_G$ be the presheaf of $\mathcal O_X$-modules with $P_G(V)=G(V)$ for opens $V\subseteq W$ and $P_G(V)=0$ otherwise, restriction maps those of $G$ between opens inside $W$ and zero otherwise, $\mathcal O_X(V)=(\mathcal O_X|_W)(V)$ acting through $G$ when $V\subseteq W$. Let $\theta_G:P_G\to P_G^\#$ be its sheafification as a presheaf of $\mathcal O_X$-modules [def-weil-presheaf-modules-sheafification]; its underlying abelian sheaf is the abelian sheafification of $P_G$. For an $\mathcal O_X$-module $H$, a morphism of presheaves of $\mathcal O_X$-modules $P_G\to H$ is the same as a morphism $G\to H|_W$ (its components on opens $V\subseteq W$; the other components are zero, and compatibility with restriction from $V\not\subseteq W$ holds because $P_G(V)=0$). With the universal property of $\theta_G$ this gives bijections $\operatorname{Hom}(P_G^\#,H)\cong\operatorname{Hom}(G,H|_W)$, natural in $G$ and $H$; so $G\mapsto P_G^\#$ is a left adjoint of restriction, and by uniqueness of left adjoints up to a unique natural isomorphism compatible with the adjunction bijections, $j_{W,!}G\cong P_G^\#$ for the left adjoint of [lem-sc-derived-open-restriction-adjunction-exact]. Under this isomorphism the counit $j_{W,!}(H|_W)\to H$ is the morphism induced by the presheaf map $P_{H|_W}\to H$ that is the identity on opens $V\subseteq W$ and zero otherwise. The underlying abelian presheaf of $P_G$ is the presheaf $j_{p!}G$ of [lem-sc-topological-extension-by-zero-stalks], so that lemma gives $(j_{W,!}G)_x=0$ for $x\notin W$ and, for $x\in W$, the isomorphism $G_x\cong(j_{W,!}G)_x$, $s_x\mapsto\theta_G(s)_x$, natural in $G$. This isomorphism is induced by the $\mathcal O_X$-linear maps $G(V)=P_G(V)\to P_G^\#(V)$ for opens $x\in V\subseteq W$, which are cofinal among the neighbourhoods of $x$, so it is $\mathcal O_{X,x}$-linear by the module structure on stalks in [def-weil-pbc-module-stalk].

source.place: Sheaves Lemma 00A7 (lemma-j-shriek-modules), clauses (2)-(3), with Definition 00A4 and the stalk calculation in Lemma 00A5

proof.text: Write $\eta^{W'}:F|_{W'}\to(j_{W',!}(F|_{W'}))|_{W'}$ for the unit of $j_{W',!}\dashv(-)|_{W'}$ [lem-sc-derived-open-restriction-adjunction-exact], with $j_{X,!}$ the identity functor and $\eta^X=\mathrm{id}_F$. For a morphism $g:F|_W\to H|_W$ of $\mathcal O_X|_W$-modules let $g^\flat:j_{W,!}(F|_W)\to H$ be its transpose, the unique morphism with $(g^\flat)|_W\circ\eta^W=g$. By definition $\iota_{W,W'}=(\eta^{W'}|_W)^\flat$. For $W'=X$ this is $(\mathrm{id}_{F|_W})^\flat$, the counit. For $W'=W$, the identity satisfies $\mathrm{id}|_W\circ\eta^W=\eta^W$, so $\iota_{W,W}=\mathrm{id}$. For $W\subseteq W'\subseteq W''$, restricting the defining identities $(\iota_{W,W'})|_W\circ\eta^W=\eta^{W'}|_W$ and $(\iota_{W',W''})|_{W'}\circ\eta^{W'}=\eta^{W''}|_{W'}$ to $W$ gives $(\iota_{W',W''}\circ\iota_{W,W'})|_W\circ\eta^W=\eta^{W''}|_W$, so $\iota_{W',W''}\circ\iota_{W,W'}$ and $\iota_{W,W''}$ are both transposes of $\eta^{W''}|_W$ and are equal by uniqueness of transposes.

source.place: Sheaves Lemma 00A7 (lemma-j-shriek-modules), clause (2), and the adjunction identities

proof.text: Let $x\in W\subseteq W'$. By Step 1 the counit $\iota_{W,X}:j_{W,!}(F|_W)\to F$ is induced by the presheaf map that is the identity on opens inside $W$ and zero otherwise, so the adjunction-map clause of [lem-sc-topological-extension-by-zero-stalks] (for the open $W$ and the underlying abelian sheaf of $F$) identifies $(\iota_{W,X})_x$ with $\mathrm{id}_{F_x}$ under the isomorphism of (1); likewise $(\iota_{W',X})_x=\mathrm{id}_{F_x}$ since $x\in W'$. By Step 2, $\iota_{W',X}\circ\iota_{W,W'}=\iota_{W,X}$, and stalk maps are functorial [def-weil-pbc-module-stalk], so $(\iota_{W',X})_x\circ(\iota_{W,W'})_x=(\iota_{W,X})_x$; hence $(\iota_{W,W'})_x=\mathrm{id}_{F_x}$ under the isomorphisms of (1) for $F|_W$ and $F|_{W'}$. Stalk maps of morphisms of $\mathcal O_X$-modules are $\mathcal O_{X,x}$-linear [def-weil-pbc-module-stalk], so this is an equality of $\mathcal O_{X,x}$-linear maps.

lean.note: Extension by zero is written out as the landed extensionByZeroPresheaf ⋙ sheafification and its adjunction is Classical.choice of open_restriction_adjunction_exact (the form of the citer open_extension_mayer_vietoris_shortExact), so iota and the counits are those of the landed adjunction. Clause (1) inside W is a natural O_{X,x}-linear isomorphism G_x ≅ (j_!G)_x of ambient stalks (scalars restricted along restrictStalkIso), tied by the germ-of-unit formula. Top-open extension is identified with the identity by the counit isomorphism, so the top transition equals the counit after that identification.
